device.name: SmartThings Hub v2
device.notes: SmartThings Hub v2 advertises local SmartThings, Edge driver, and Matter services via mDNS. The primary identity is the _smartthings._tcp TXT id value. _smartthings-hedge._tcp on port 8766 exposes Edge driver control features, and _matter._tcp advertises the hub's Matter operational node endpoint — the hub is a Matter CONTROLLER only, not a bridge: attached Zigbee/Z-Wave devices are not exposed to other Matter fabrics (no bridge-to-third-party-fabrics shipped through firmware 0.57.x). Security note: Cisco Talos disclosed 20 vulnerabilities (incl. RCE chains) in SmartThings Hub firmware 0.20.17 in 2018 (TALOS-2018-0539 … TALOS-2018-0581). Going local: where this hub is on the LAN, the Samsung appliances on the same account usually are too, and for those a cloud-free route exists. The LocalThings Home Assistant integration (HACS, domain `localthings`) drives Samsung SmartThings-compatible washers, dryers, refrigerators, air conditioners, ovens and similar appliances directly over the LAN — OCF resources over CoAP/DTLS with a locally minted client certificate (older 2018–2022 units: HTTPS on TCP 8888) — and needs Samsung's servers only once, unauthenticated, for the first appliance. It does NOT drive this hub or the Zigbee/Z-Wave devices paired to it; those stay on the hub (or move to a local coordinator). A consumer that sees this hub and a Home Assistant server on the same network should point the user at LocalThings rather than at the cloud SmartThings integration.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: Nothing is done at the hub. The welcome code on its underside claims the hub into a Samsung account during setup ("Redeem the welcome code into a Samsung account"). That is account binding, not client pairing, and it also needs the cloud.

pairing.notes: Every local port this hub serves is behind a cloud-issued credential. This project's probe of a real hub got 401 UnauthorizedError from both 8766 and 9495 without a bearer token. The token itself comes from the official CLI's source and the vendor app's behaviour, and a working authorised call has not been made here. The CLI also pins the hub's TLS certificate, whose CN embeds the hub's UUID. If Samsung's cloud goes, no new client can be authorised, which is why this spec is identify_only. Joining Zigbee, Z-Wave and Matter devices to the hub is a separate network join run from the SmartThings app.

pin.notes: Not a code but a bearer token, and it comes from Samsung's cloud, not from the hub. The official SmartThings CLI sends the signed-in account's OAuth token to the driver-log API on port 9495. Per the vendor app's diagnostics flow, the Edge API on port 8766 takes a per-hub token that the cloud API issues to a signed-in client. No local exchange, button or printed code yields either one.

unpair.notes: The tokens belong to the Samsung account, so revoking one is presumably an account-side action (sign out, or revoke the app's access). Whether the hub notices, and how quickly, is not established. A factory reset unclaims the hub entirely.

factory_reset.effect: Unclaims the hub and clears its ZigBee/Z-Wave networks; every paired radio device must be re-joined afterwards.

procedures.indicator: Status LED turns yellow and flashes.
procedures.name: Reset button held while powering on

steps.action: Hold the recessed reset button on the back while restoring power, and keep holding until the LED flashes yellow.
steps.notes: Vendor-documented; verify before use — this drops every paired ZigBee and Z-Wave device.

methods.description: The hub reaches the LAN over Ethernet and is then bound to a Samsung account with the welcome code printed on its underside, receiving its identity and driver set from there. The second phase is not optional and there is no documented way to skip it — local Edge drivers run on the hub afterwards, but the hub has to be claimed first.
methods.name: Ethernet, then redeem the welcome code

stages.description: Ethernet to the router; the hub takes a DHCP lease and advertises _smartthings._tcp.local.
stages.name: Get the hub onto the LAN

steps.action: Connect Ethernet, insert the batteries if fitted, and apply power.
steps.expect: Status LED settles to solid green once the hub reaches the service.

cloud.local_alternative: None known. Edge drivers execute locally once installed, but the claim step and driver distribution both require the cloud.

stages.description: The welcome code on the hub is redeemed in the vendor app, which binds the hub to a Samsung account and provisions its drivers.
stages.name: Redeem the welcome code into a Samsung account

steps.action: Redeem the welcome code printed on the underside of the hub in the vendor app.

setup.notes: The hub is Ethernet-only and its onboarding is entirely cloud-mediated: the welcome code printed on the underside is redeemed against Samsung's service, and the hub receives its identity and driver set from there. Local Edge drivers run on the hub afterwards, but there is no documented way to claim an unclaimed hub without the cloud, which is the key risk if the service is retired — and there is precedent: Samsung shut down the hub v1 cloud on 2021-06-30, rendering those hubs useless.

rejoin.notes: Moving the hub to a different router is a cable move; the cloud claim is unaffected.

testing.notes: Probed live 2026-08-14 against the real hub (id D052A80000000001 at the address its mDNS answers resolved to). All three documented mDNS services re-observed exactly as recorded in evidence (2026-07-16): _smartthings._tcp 8081 (type=hubv2, path=/), _smartthings-hedge._tcp 8766 (feat=ctrl), _matter._tcp 49722 (T=6). The hedge HTTPS service is REAL and gated as documented: GET /devices/hub/connectionState on 8766 without a bearer token answers 401 {"error":{"code":"UnauthorizedError","message":"authentication is required for rate limited endpoints"}}, and its TLS certificate CN embeds the hub UUID (hla-tcp.<hub-uuid>.st, matching the hedge instance name) — corroborating the CLI's cert-pinning behavior. Port 9495 (CLI logcat API) answers the same 401 JSON with an O=SmartThings Inc. self-signed cert. Port 8081, despite being the advertised primary service, REFUSED both http and https connections during the probe — see the endpoint note. Not exercised: anything behind the cloud-issued bearer tokens, and the reboot POST (deliberately).

helpful_urls.description: The recommended route off the SmartThings cloud for the Samsung appliances on this hub's account (washers, dryers, refrigerators, air conditioners, ovens and more): a HACS integration, domain `localthings`, that talks to each appliance over the LAN (OCF over CoAP/DTLS; HTTPS on TCP 8888 for 2018–2022 units) with no Samsung account. It does not drive the hub itself or its Zigbee/Z-Wave children. Install in one tap with https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/hacs_repository/?owner=mbillow&repository=localthings&category=integration

http_endpoints.description: Primary _smartthings._tcp service endpoint on port 8081 (probe-observed only; the 2016 community capture's TXT path=/ supports a root path existing, but no public documentation of an HTTP API on 8081 exists). Edge control is advertised separately on the hedge HTTPS service. Live probe 2026-08-14 (firmware-current hub, id D052A80000000001): the port REFUSED both http and https connections even while the mDNS answer advertising it was fresh — on current firmware nothing listens there, so treat the advertisement as legacy identity metadata, not a usable API.
http_endpoints.name: SmartThings Local Service Root

http_endpoints.description: App-derived, not exercised on hardware: hedge HTTPS endpoint used by the vendor app's hub diagnostics flow. Authenticated with a cloud-issued HubEdgeAuthentication bearer token (see smartthings_local_protocol.edge_driver_service.auth).
http_endpoints.name: Hub Connection State (hedge, port 8766)

http_endpoints.description: App-derived, not exercised on hardware: hedge HTTPS endpoint returning the hub's diagnostic logs, same bearer auth as /devices/hub/connectionState.
http_endpoints.name: Diagnostic Logs Download (hedge, port 8766)

http_endpoints.description: App-derived, not exercised on hardware: hedge HTTPS endpoint that reboots the hub, same bearer auth as /devices/hub/connectionState.
http_endpoints.name: Hub Reboot (hedge, port 8766)

http_endpoints.description: Undocumented local HTTPS API on port 9495 used by the official SmartThings CLI (edge:drivers:logcat). Requires Samsung OAuth bearer headers; TLS server certificate pinned to the hub identity.
http_endpoints.name: Edge Drivers (port 9495)

http_endpoints.description: Server-Sent Events live log stream on port 9495, same OAuth + TLS pinning as /drivers (official CLI logcat.ts).
http_endpoints.name: Edge Driver Logs SSE (port 9495)

cloud_hedge_api.notes: App-derived, not hardware-verified: the vendor app also speaks a cloud-side "hedge" API family for Matter and Thread management (MatterService) — e.g. /hedge/request/{hubId}/devices/{deviceId}/matter/fabrics, /hedge/request/{hubId}/matter/rendezvous, and /hedge/request/{hubId}/thread/networkInfo — plus Matter DCL vendor/product lookups. These are cloud REST endpoints reached through Samsung's backend, not endpoints served by the hub itself.

auth.notes: App-derived: requests carry an Authorization: Bearer header built from a cloud-issued HubEdgeAuthentication (access_token plus a client public certificate), obtained from the cloud API via POST /hubdevices/{hubDeviceId}/hedge/auth.

edge_driver_service.confidence_notes: App-derived, not exercised on hardware: the vendor app's hub diagnostics flow discovers _smartthings-hedge._tcp.local. via mDNS and matches the endpoint against its L3_HTTPS protocol, then talks to it through a plain Retrofit HTTPS interface (iv/d). The feat=ctrl TXT key remains probe-only — the app never reads the hedge TXT record.
edge_driver_service.notes: Service and port are corroborated by community observation (Nov 2024) and by the vendor app's mDNS discovery. The transport is HTTPS, not WebSocket: the app classifies the discovered endpoint as an HTTPS diagnostics protocol. The feat=ctrl TXT key rests solely on this spec's own probe — treat it as unverified.

local_https_api.notes: Undocumented local API used by the official SmartThings CLI (edge:drivers:logcat, defaultLiveLogPort = 9495): GET /drivers and GET /drivers/logs (Server-Sent Events), authenticated with Samsung OAuth bearer headers; the CLI pins the hub's TLS server certificate against its identity. Source: SmartThingsCommunity/smartthings-cli src/commands/edge/drivers/logcat.ts.

matter_controller.notes: Hub v2 is a CSA-certified Matter CONTROLLER (not a bridge — see device notes). TXT T=6 is the Matter operational-discovery kTcpSupported bitmask (TCP client + server). Port 49722 is probe-observed only: Matter operational discovery uses ephemeral ports, so treat it as instance-specific, not normative.
